Subject: EchoWell pilot — synthesis, technical asks, and proposed kickoff window

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick synthesis from our side and a proposed path to get the pilot started. I captured the main pain points, the target goals, and a short list of technical asks so engineering can scope the POC.

High-level pain & goals (what you told us)
- Current triage assistant returns noisy results and long tail hallucinations when pulling from the knowledge base (clinical notes + policies).
- Need deterministic reranking and a lightweight streaming assistant for live agent support.
- Goal: 80% reduction in irrelevant highlights; sub-300ms tail latency for live surfacing to agents.

Proposed pilot scope (2–4 weeks)
- Integration: embeddings + candidate rerank pipeline (batch embed, async rerank service).
- Real-time: streaming generation with function-calling for structured, agent-facing cards.
- SDK surface: minimal client change — one streaming SDK hook + a JSON function schema for card generation.

Technical asks for your team (so our engineers can build the MAP and POC):
1) Example KB snapshot (CSV or newline-delimited JSON) — ~10k records is fine as a sample.
2) A short list of 6–8 representative queries/prompts you want to validate against (we'll include these in evals).
3) Any data residency or encryption constraints (we heard EU-based data for some accounts; flag if any EchoWell customers are affected).
4) Security contact for SOC2 questionnaire follow-up (we can send a link to our security portal).

Redwood deliverables for pilot
- Sandbox API keys + sample pipeline config.
- Small SDK patch (streaming hook + function-call schema) and example client.
- Simple confidence & rerank dashboard (token-level latency + rerank precision on the example prompts).

Proposed timeline
- Confirm sample data + security contact by Jul 23.
- Kickoff (remote): week of Aug 2 — 60–90 minute tech kickoff + MAP sign-off.
- Pilot run: Aug 3–Aug 21 (instrumented POC, weekly check-ins).

Next steps
- Alex: confirm data delivery cadence and who owns the security questionnaire.
- Priya: confirm which tenant(s) we should instrument for the POC.
- Ben / Sergio: will draft the SDK diff and a short example function schema by EOD Jul 20.

Attachments: referenced benchmark doc (we'll share the relevant sections in the sandbox).

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / Sergio — high level tech plan and concrete SDK notes below. Putting this here so Alex/Priya can see what to expect from engineering.

1) SDK footprint
- We'll produce a 2-file patch: (1) streaming client hook (language: JS + Python example) and (2) a small util for function-call schema validation.
- Backwards compatible: if a customer doesn't adopt streaming, the call falls back to short-poll generation.

2) Function-calling schema (example)
- We recommend a compact JSON schema for agent cards:
  {"title":"string","priority":"low|med|high","highlights":[{"start":int,"end":int,"score":float}],"action":{"type":"open_url","url":"string"}}
- We'll include a small serializer in the SDK to enforce stable structured output.

3) Streaming and fallback logic
- Primary: WebSocket streaming with per-token deltas and an inline function-call token when a card completes.
- Fallback: if stream latency > 400ms for 3 consecutive tokens, client automatically switches to a compact completion that returns a precomputed card.

4) Embeddings + rerank path
- Batch embed the KB snapshot in our sandbox (use 1536-d float embeddings) and provision a rerank service that computes MIPS cosine scores + a learned reranker for the top-50 candidates.
- We'll expose a simple REST endpoint for candidate scoring so EchoWell can run a local replica for evaluation.

5) Security & observability
- We'll attach token-level latency logs and event traces to the sandbox—no customer PII will leave the provided anonymized snapshot.

Action items I will own
- Draft SDK diff and example function schema by EOD Jul 20 (will post to the Drive link in the MAP).
- Prepare a sandbox with streaming+function-call enabled and a short runbook for Alex to exercise latency tests.
